world.title: Palestinians told to leave homes in village where Israeli settlers besieged houses
world.description: The mayor of Qusra says Israeli troops have been telling families to leave their houses, using some as barracks.

world.title: Romania shuts only nuclear plant as heat causes huge drop in Danube River level
world.description: The Cernavodă plant, which produces 20% of Romania's electricity, is not expected to be restarted within the next 10 days.

world.title: Putin can no longer claim victory in Ukraine, Nobel Peace Prize winner tells BBC
world.description: In an exclusive interview with the BBC’s Steve Rosenberg, Dmitry Muratov says the Kremlin leader can only "destroy Ukraine, not conquer it", with the war now in its fifth year.

world.title: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms
world.description: Thousands of sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

world.title: Person fined after using foghorn to wake sleeping polar bear
world.description: Under local regulations in the region, "it is forbidden to needlessly disturb, attract or pursue a polar bear".

world.title: Eurovision Song Contest 2027 to be held in Burgas, Bulgaria
world.description: The Black Sea location has been selected after Bulgarian singer Dara won this year's contest.

world.title: Mangione lawyers to meet federal prosecutors amid reports of plea deal
world.description: Mangione faces two federal charges of stalking resulting in death, each carrying a maximum sentence of life in prison.

world.title: Family of Irish plane crash victim awarded $29m in damages
world.description: A jury in Chicago in the US awarded the sum to Michael Ryan's family after his  widow Naoise Connolly Ryan brought a civil suit against Boeing.

world.title: Air India to test all pilots for banned substances
world.description: It comes after one of its planes suddenly lost altitude last week, with a number of passengers injured.

world.title: Four Canadian hockey stars remain suspended after sexual assault acquittal
world.description: A fifth has been reinstated, though an appeals board found that the whole group broke Hockey Canada's code of conduct.

world.title: Ebola outbreak on track to be deadliest ever, WHO chief says
world.description: The outbreak, declared on 15 May, has caused more than 2,000 deaths, with thousands more reported cases.

world.title: Presidential pardon for French alleged spy accused of plotting Mali coup
world.description: France is yet to comment on Yann Vezilier's pardon and previously called the accusations "unfounded".

world.title: Travis Kelce shares first details from his wedding to Taylor Swift: 'Best night of my life'
world.description: In the comments, Kelce called Swift his "wife" for first time and said it was a "childhood dream" to wed at Madison Square Garden.

world.title: French ambassador to CAR accused of misconduct at official residence faces disciplinary action
world.description: The accusations against Bruno Foucher prompted investigations into a potential security breach.

world.title: BTS star V reveals hearing loss battle during livestream
world.description: The K-pop star says he has suffered hearing issues for over two years before revealing it publicly this week.

US.title: Kennedy Center Board votes again to shut main building down — and add Trump's name back
US.description: The board voted to close the Washington, D.C., arts complex's main campus for a $250 million renovation — three months after a federal judge temporarily blocked a similar closure.

US.title: Mangione could plead guilty in federal case ahead of N.Y. murder trial
US.description: A surprise hearing this Friday in federal court has added to speculation that Luigi Mangione could enter a plea, which could derail a state murder trial.

US.title: Vladimir Putin's first visit to disputed Pacific islands draws Tokyo protest
US.description: The four southernmost islands of the chain also are claimed by Japan, which calls them the Northern Territories.

US.title: By sky and sea, Ukraine's drone strikes challenge Russia's grip on Crimea
US.description: Russia maintained an iron grip on Crimea since seizing it from Ukraine in 2014. Many Russian civilians go there to enjoy the beaches. But now Ukraine is hitting Crimea hard, upending daily life.

US.title: Taiwan briefly slows its mobile internet to text-only speed as part of defense drill
US.description: The drills come amid rising tensions with China, which frequently sends military planes and ships towards Taiwan.

US.title: Inflation eased slightly in July. And, ICE plans to give officers electric shock gloves
US.description: Inflation cooled a bit last month, according to a new report from the Labor Department. And, ICE plans to equip its officers with electric shock gloves.

US.title: The drug lenacapavir is a mighty weapon against HIV. Its rollout gets mixed reviews
US.description: It's a twice-a-year injection that is remarkably effective in preventing an HIV infection. Distribution is starting. But questions are being raised about getting it to the areas that need it most

US.title: Primary voters send mixed signals about what they want from the Democratic Party
US.description: Primary results this month in Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin paint a muddled picture of just how far to the left Democratic voters want their candidates to be come this fall's midterm election

US.title: U.S. ambassador calls settler siege of Palestinian homes a 'horrific act of terror'
US.description: The U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemned the actions of Jewish settlers who are besieging the home of an American Palestinian family in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

US.title: These swing voters in Nevada say they are not dismissing socialist candidates
US.description: In online focus groups, 10 of 12 Biden-to-Trump voters said they wouldn't automatically think negatively of a politician who identifies with socialism.
